the proposed process variation sensor has a high sensitivity of 2.3 X compared to the above- threshold operation and a low power consumption of 2.5 nW.
a bias-free, low power and high-sensitivity process monitoring sensor has been designed, fabricated and characterized in a 65nm CMOS technology.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed sub-threshold based process variation sensor is a promising candidate for low-power, bias-independent and high-sensitivity applications.
the proposed sub-threshold sensor design has demonstrated the capability to measure the random threshold voltage variation in the 65 nm bulk process with a sensitivity of 0.4 mV/µm.
the proposed sensor has been able to accurately detect random process variation in the threshold voltage with a sensitivity of 1.5 mV/μm and 0.6 mV/μ m for the PMOS and NMOS devices, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed sub-threshold based sensor design is highly sensitive, low-power, and is able to monitor process variation across a large area on the chip.
the process variation sensor is capable of detecting the process variations in a single chip without the need of any external reference device.
the sub-threshold operation of MOSFETs can be utilized to develop high-sensitivity process monitors for random variations in the transistor threshold voltages.
